seoTitle: How to Share Documents in a Microsoft Teams Meeting (2026)
metaDescription: Attach and co-edit a file live during a Teams meeting through the chat panel, check the sharing permission before you send it, and find it again afterward in the renamed Shared tab.
intro: Getting everyone looking at the same document during a live call works best when you can attach it without pausing to send a separate email. This guide covers opening the chat panel tied to a meeting, attaching a file, checking who's allowed to view or edit it before it sends, and where it ends up once the call is over. It's built for anyone running client calls or team reviews in Teams who's tired of switching windows to send an attachment.

steps.heading: Open the chat tied to your meeting
steps.body: Every Teams meeting has its own chat thread, reachable from the Chat tab at the top of the meeting window. File sharing happens here, through the same message box used to type a note to attendees, not through a separate transfer tool. Anything attached becomes part of the permanent meeting record, visible to anyone in the conversation whether they joined the call or not.

steps.heading: Find the attach files control
steps.body: Along the bottom of the message box sits a row of icons: emoji, attach, GIF, sticker, and more. Hovering over the paperclip icon pops up an "Attach files" tooltip. Microsoft's own documentation frames this as the Actions and apps menu (the plus icon) followed by Attach file, so if your version shows a menu instead of a bare paperclip, that's the same control under a different entry point. Either way, clicking it opens your options for where the file comes from: something already sitting in OneDrive, or a local file you haven't uploaded anywhere yet.

image.caption: The message box toolbar in a meeting chat, with the Attach files tooltip showing over the paperclip icon.

steps.heading: Check the permission line before sending
steps.body: Once a file is picked, it shows up as a preview card above the message box before anything sends: a filename, a thumbnail, and a line underneath stating exactly who can do what with it, such as "Anyone with the link can edit." Read that line instead of skimming past it. Microsoft's default for a file attached this way is People currently in this chat, meaning it's the real access level the file gets the second it lands, not a placeholder to configure later.

image.caption: A file staged in the message box before sending, showing its name and the current sharing permission: here, anyone with the link can edit it.

steps.heading: Tighten permissions for sensitive files
steps.body: If the default is broader than you want, change it before the message goes out. Click the permission line on the preview card to switch between Can edit, Can review, Can view, or Can't download, or to restrict access to specific people, useful if external guests are on the call and shouldn't get a wide-open link.

steps.heading: Send it and watch it land in the thread
steps.body: Select send and the file appears as a compact card with a thumbnail and timestamp, sitting in the message flow like any other message. Anyone in the meeting or chat can open it straight from there, with no separate download step and no hunting through email for a buried attachment.

image.caption: A shared image sent into the meeting chat, appearing as a timestamped card directly in the conversation.

steps.heading: Open the file for real-time co-authoring
steps.body: For Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files, clicking the shared file opens it inside Teams itself instead of a separate app, and multiple attendees can type into it at once with each person's cursor visible. That's the advantage over emailing a copy around: one live document everyone edits together instead of several versions that need merging afterward.

steps.heading: Find it again after the call ends
steps.body: You don't have to scroll back through chat to relocate a file. Open the chat and select the Shared tab. Microsoft renamed this from Files to Shared, so older screenshots and guides may still show the previous name. It lists every file and link posted in that conversation, searchable separately from links, and each channel also keeps its own SharePoint library behind the same tab.

troubleshooting.problem: A file fails to send in a large meeting chat
troubleshooting.cause: Microsoft's own troubleshooting documentation covers this: when a chat has more than 100 participants, the default People currently in this chat link type requires each viewer to individually request access, and the send can fail outright.
troubleshooting.fix: Click the file's current sharing setting before sending and switch it to Anyone (if the chat includes people outside your organization) or People in your organization. If neither option is available, an admin has to enable it in the SharePoint admin center.

troubleshooting.problem: The Files tab from an older guide doesn't exist anymore
troubleshooting.cause: Microsoft renamed it to Shared in both channels and chats.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the chat and look for Shared instead: same content, new label.

troubleshooting.problem: An external guest can't open a file that was shared
troubleshooting.cause: The permission was left on a setting that only covers people already in the chat or inside the organization.
troubleshooting.fix: Reopen the file's sharing settings from its card and switch to a link type that includes guests, or add the specific person by name.

faq.question: Can multiple people edit a shared document at the same time in a Teams meeting?
faq.answer: Yes. Opening a Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file inside Teams instead of downloading it supports real-time co-authoring, with every attendee's cursor visible as they type.

faq.question: How do I let an external guest access a file I share?
faq.answer: Check the permission line on the file's preview card before sending, and switch it to a setting that includes people outside your organization, or name the specific guest directly.

faq.question: Where do shared files go after the meeting ends?
faq.answer: Open the chat and select Shared, the tab Microsoft used to call Files, to see every file and link posted during that call without scrolling back through messages.

faq.question: Can I share a file from OneDrive without downloading it first?
faq.answer: Yes. The attach files option lets you pick a file already stored in OneDrive directly, with no local copy required.

faq.question: Why did my file fail to send in a big meeting chat?
faq.answer: Past 100 participants, the default sharing link requires individual access requests and can fail to send at all. Switching the file's sharing setting to Anyone or People in your organization before sending fixes it.
